Looking at the observed failure: The help panel (offcanvas) is open and has role="dialog" with aria-modal="true". The focus is trapped in the help panel - when tabbing from #help-close, it goes back to #help (the dialog) instead of reaching #amount field.

The issue is in the offcanvas.js _enforceFocusOnElement method which forces focus back to the offcanvas element when focus leaves it. This is modal behavior, but the panel is described as "non-modal" in the task goal.

Looking at the HTML: the offcanvas has `data-bs-backdrop="false"` and `data-bs-scroll="true"` - this suggests it's not a true modal (no backdrop, allows scrolling). However, the offcanvas.js still enforces focus trap via _enforceFocusOnElement.

The fix should be to not enforce focus trap when the offcanvas is not modal (i.e., when backdrop is false or scroll is true). Let me check the config options: backdrop, keyboard, scroll.

In the show() method, it sets aria-modal="true" and role="dialog" regardless. But for a non-modal panel, it shouldn't trap focus.

The repair strategy: Modify the _enforceFocusOnElement method to only enforce focus when the offcanvas is truly modal (backdrop=true and scroll=false). Or better, check if it's a non-modal panel (backdrop=false or scroll=true) and skip focus enforcement.

The config has: backdrop (default true), keyboard (default true), scroll (default false).

In the HTML, the offcanvas has `data-bs-backdrop="false"` and `data-bs-scroll="true"`. So config.backdrop=false, config.scroll=true.

The fix: In _enforceFocusOnElement, only enforce focus if this._config.backdrop === true && this._config.scroll === false (i.e., truly modal). Otherwise, don't trap focus.
